Subject: Post-demo: API access patterns & implementation checklist

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can loop in your infra team and get a small pilot running next month.

Recap of what we demo'd
- High-level: Redwood hosted API + Dedicated routing option for production traffic; SDK + server and browser clients.
- Key features relevant to GreenBridge: structured output/tool-calling (for ledger enrichment), embeddings + reranker for search relevance, and routing policies for cost vs latency.

Recommended access/auth pattern (proposal)
1) Server-to-server (core app, ingestion pipelines)
   - Use a Redwood service account (customer-managed) that issues short-lived JWT access tokens (1h) via your identity broker.
   - Keep long-term credential material inside your KMS; Redwood will accept signed JWTs to mint scoped tokens if you prefer not to store API keys in your backend.
2) Browser/mobile clients (end-user features)
   - Do NOT embed long-lived API keys. Use an app-auth layer that mints ephemeral tokens with limited scope (read-only embeddings or completion tokens with low rate).
3) Internal automation (batch jobs)
   - Use rotated API keys with automatic rotation every 30 days + rotation webhook to notify your secrets manager.

Implementation notes & tradeoffs
- Service accounts + JWTs: best for security and rotation, small infra work to integrate with your identity provider.
- API keys for backend: easiest to get started but needs rotation and KMS storage.
- OAuth for delegated user access: relevant only if you plan to attribute requests to end users.

Open items we should cover on the follow-up call
- Which flow will own embeddings creation (your ingestion vs. Redwood side)?
- Do you have an existing identity broker that can sign JWTs? (e.g., Keycloak, Vault, STS)
- Compliance: do you need a dedicated VPC/private deployment for production?

Attachments: sending an architecture diagram + an auth requirements sheet that lists recommended headers, token lifetimes, and an example JWT assertion flow (redwood-integration-arch-v1.png, auth-requirements.xlsx). Also attaching a draft SOW template we can adapt.

Proposed next steps
1) Engineering sync (30m) next week: technical owners from GreenBridge + Karthik + me to walk through token minting and routing policy.
2) Pilot scope: proof-of-concept for embeddings + reranker on a single dataset, 2-week run.
3) Draft SOW and procurement checklist from Monica.

If that looks right, I can send a calendar invite for a 30-minute deep-dive and drop the Drive link with the artifacts.

Sarah — great questions. Short answers up front, then an action plan and the JWT snippet you can drop into Vault's "JWT/OIDC" pipeline.

1) Rotation/support: Redwood supports a rotation API and a webhook pattern. You can push new keys via the Redwood Admin API (POST /v1/keys) and we also emit rotation events to an endpoint you register. We'll share the webhook schema in the Drive link. For Vault we typically recommend the ephemeral API key pattern: Vault requests a short-lived API token from Redwood for a job, and Vault rotates the secret material behind the scenes.

2) JWT claims enforcement: yes — we validate aud, iss, exp, and custom scope claims. You can configure per-client scopes so an embeddings token only has the embeddings:write or embeddings:read scope. We also support model-level scoping (e.g., restrict tokens to the "embed-v2" model).

3) Dedicated vs hosted: Dedicated capacity handles inference runtime; the control plane (billing/observability) remains hosted unless you request Private deployment. You can route traffic to Dedicated pools while retaining the hosted console and analytics. If you need VPC peering or on-prem data residency we can discuss Private.

4) Throughput/quotas: for a pilot sized like yours (1M tokens ingestion, 200k embeddings) we recommend a small Dedicated pool or burst-enabled hosted tier. Soft quotas: embeddings ingestion throughput ~2000 embeddings/minute on a single accelerator; generation throughput depends on model and sequence length — we'll size the pool during the infra sync.

Example JWT assertion (minimal) — drop-in for Vault JWT auth plugin:

-----BEGIN SNIPPET-----
POST /oauth/token HTTP/1.1
Host: auth.greenbridge.internal
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer&assertion=<BASE64URL(JWT)>&scope=embeddings:write

# JWT claims (example)
{
  "iss": "greenbridge-iam@example.com",
  "sub": "svc-embeddings@greenbridge.ai",
  "aud": "https://api.redwood.com/token",
  "exp": 1624665600,
  "scope": "embeddings:write model:embed-v2"
}
-----END SNIPPET-----
